Count Wrongula - Album 1: WHO

To Whom It May Concern

"To whom it may concern"

[Rubato Intro]

Afternoon tea Western sun Porcelain waiting The day half done

One measured spoon A civilized cup Newspaper open Let’s see who’s messed up

[Verse 1]

Front page misery, column number four Feeding shortages hitting the poor Market shelves thinning, traders complain Sources constrained and the prices insane

Some travel freely wherever they choose Some follow instincts they cannot refuse Some never crossed, some never can Some lost the instinct no one understands

Now traders are charging whatever they please For marrow and morsels and species-specific needs The wealthy still dine The desperate wait

Funny how hunger Can recognize one’s estate

[Pre-Chorus]

Supply goes down The numbers rise Another neat excuse in bureaucratic disguise Wrongula sighs And turns the page

The world has apparently Misplaced its brain

[Chorus]

To whom it may concern Apparently nobody has a name Stamp it, seal it, send it out And call indifference a game

To whom it may concern Such an elegant little phrase Pass the problem desk to desk While the starving learn to pay

Pour another cup Surely someone will look up

Eventually

[Verse 2]

Soft steps enter, flour on a sleeve Tisha from kitchens has something to leave Young for a witch at two-twenty years Still new enough to tolerate everyone here

Black heavy envelope Thirteen seals red Wrongula lowers The news he has read

The Tridecagon of Old Thirteen vampires enthroned Eight hundred years deciding What everyone should have known

He turns the letter His eyebrow ascends

There on the front The insult begins

To Whom It May Concern

His smile becomes terribly refined

[Pre-Chorus]

They know who I am They know where I live They know every title etiquette can give

And after eight centuries This is their art?

Apparently manners Have fallen apart

[Chorus]

To whom it may concern Thirteen fossils dressed in lace Eight hundred years in velvet chairs And still they cannot address a face

To whom it may concern What a beautifully polished slight Invite a Count without the Count Then summon him tonight

Seal it in red Letter it gold Nothing says respect Like bureaucracy old

Concern has arrived

[Bridge]

He breaks the seals Unfolds the page

An audience requested Attendance expected Formal dress preferred

Naturally

Not the summons Not the hall Not their ancient council call

Of every offense Large and small

It’s the greeting Most of all

[Final Chorus]

To whom it may concern Fine, consider me concerned You called without the courtesy But courtesy can be returned

Let them stare Let them pry Let them wonder what and why

Why I breakfast Why I dine Why the daylight suits me fine

If they wanted my attention They have managed that at last

[Vamp Outro]

He folds the letter neatly Sets it by the tea Thirteen crimson seals Staring back at me

One final sip One irritated grin

“Fine. I’ll go.”

He looks again at the greeting

To whom it may concern

Savages
